title: Faith
hook: faith is the substance of things hoped for
tomorrow: what's the difference between hope and wishful thinking?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Thérèse's little way: a small thing measured by the love inside it. The line was little things, great love. Today the last stretch begins: the summit, and three things that remain, starting with faith.

Nobody tests a chair before sitting in it. You get into a car with a driver you met thirty seconds ago. You eat food a stranger cooked. Whole days run on trust you never proved. The Letter to the Hebrews gives faith a definition, in the Douay-Rheims: "Now faith is the substance of things to be hoped for, the evidence of things that appear not." Evidence of what you can't see. So where does that come from? Catholics have two honest answers, and they pull in different directions.
screen: `NOBODY TESTS THE CHAIR.` → `THE EVIDENCE OF THINGS UNSEEN.` → `TWO HONEST ANSWERS.`

segments.voice: The first answer: faith is a gift. You can't argue yourself into it or work it up by trying harder. The Catechism calls it a gift of God, a virtue he pours in. The best case for this view is real: it explains why two people can hear the same reasons and only one believes, and it takes the pressure off. Nobody earns it. The second answer: faith is a choice. The same Catechism says believing is a truly human act, free, never forced, and not against reason. The best case here is real too: it treats the believer as a person who says yes, not a container that got filled. Thomas Aquinas puts the mind and the will together: the mind agrees, because the will, moved by grace, chooses to. So which is it? Mark's Gospel has a father with a sick son who answers in one breath, in the Douay-Rheims: "I do believe, Lord: help my unbelief." I do believe: that's his choice. Help my unbelief: that's asking for the gift. Here's one to tell a friend tonight: the Creed Catholics say at Mass doesn't begin with God exists. It begins with I believe, a person speaking.
screen: `FAITH IS A GIFT.` · `FAITH IS A FREE CHOICE.` · `I DO BELIEVE, HELP MY UNBELIEF.` · `THE CREED STARTS WITH A PERSON.` · then, large: `I BELIEVE.`

segments.voice: Say the two words out loud, quietly: I believe. Then add one thing you can honestly put after them, anything at all. If you pray, the Creed's own opening is yours: I believe in God; and if part of you doubts, the father's words fit right beside it: help my unbelief.
Faith. The evidence of things unseen, which Catholics call both God's gift and a free yes.
Carry this: I believe, two small words with a whole person standing behind them. Until tomorrow.
